title: When an Institution Must Stop Speaking for a Claim
thesis: An institution offering continuing assessment of challenges must retain dependable capacity to provide it or qualify its offer, even when its original conclusion remains justified.
contribution: Separates evidence preservation from delegation of continuing inquiry, specifying public role criteria, practical response capacity and a withdrawal that need not retract the proposition.
strongest_objection: The principle applies a general duty against misrepresenting services rather than establishing an independent epistemic norm; the final accepts this and defends the narrower analysis.
originality_limitations: Bounded excerpt-based literature coverage; Kukla is a close predecessor; no demonstrated priority.
open_questions: How do disputed public conventions fix the offered role?
What reliability and notice suffice in borderline cases?
When does lost oversight supply additional evidence defeating confidence?
sources: Almagro et al. 2023, abstract and introduction
revision_provenance: Fresh successor AI editor after pause; original draft and identity preserved; one revision answering both reviews; no new source reading.
